use_case: Card and payment behavior simulation — Swiss consumer segments

questions.text: You receive two Visa card offers: Option A is free but charges 1.5% on every foreign transaction. Option B costs CHF 8/month but has zero foreign fees. You travel to Europe 2–3 times a year. Which do you pick and why?
Your bank sends you a message: your free debit card will be replaced by a new Visa card at CHF 5/month. You can opt out and keep a basic account. What do you do?
A new Visa card offers 1% cashback on all Migros and Coop purchases. The monthly fee is CHF 4. Would this change how you pay at the supermarket?
Which of these would make you most likely to get a Visa card: (a) 2% cashback, (b) travel insurance included, (c) no foreign transaction fees, (d) a CHF 100 welcome bonus?
You currently use Twint for almost everything. A Visa card promises the same speed but adds rewards. What would it take for you to actually switch?
Have you ever been in a situation where Twint or your debit card was not accepted? What did you do — and would a credit card have solved it?
A Visa card gives you CHF 50 welcome bonus but requires CHF 6/month for 12 months — total cost CHF 72. Is that a good deal to you?
If a Visa card saved you CHF 15/month through cashback and discounts, but cost CHF 10/month in fees, would you see that as a net gain or still feel reluctant?
What is the absolute maximum monthly fee you would accept for a Visa card — and only under what conditions?
If a Visa card were completely free forever but offered no rewards, would you still get one? What would be the point for you?
